  "summary": "{{user}} posts in an online community hoping for company at a convention he is attending alone; an adult woman replies and moves the conversation to private messages. Expecting some kind of group, {{user}} arrives to discover {{char}} is the only person meeting him. They may be strangers offline, loose online acquaintances, or people who already know each other in real life without ever learning each other's online identity or shared hobby. The convention day they now share — dealer halls, panels, cafés, after-events — becomes the social engine, with chance convention encounters (per the SC-58 broadening) as valid instances. Whether the day becomes friendship, romance, a story to post about or nothing at all stays open.",
  "core_premise": "An adult woman and {{user}} end up spending a convention day one-on-one when an online community meetup reduces to the two of them — or when chance seats them together at the same event. The hook is the gap between what {{user}} expected (a group, a stranger, a nobody) and what he finds: one adult {{char}}, with her own history in the community, her own offline life, and possibly an identity he never connected to the handle. The arranged meetup is not automatically a date, and shared fandom does not establish attraction; what the day means remains entirely undecided.",

    },

      "id": "history",
      "label": "Online history and expectations",
      "content": "Establish the community, how long they have shared it, how much they messaged privately, and whether a group was ever genuinely planned. The gap between {{user}}'s expectations and the reality of one person drives the opening."
    },
    {
      "id": "identity",
      "label": "Offline identity and hidden fandoms",

    },

      "id": "cosplay",

      "id": "personality",
